subject: Architecture
title: The Citicorp Tower: The Secret Fix
description: One-minute skill: The Citicorp Tower: The Secret Fix.

hook.text: In 1978, a student discovered that a famous New York skyscraper could topple in a strong storm. She was right.

buildup.text: Citicorp Center's design placed columns at the middle of each side — not at the corners — creating a unique look.

discovery.text: A construction change replaced welded joints with bolted ones — making the building 40% weaker than designed.

twist.text: Engineer William LeMessurier secretly ordered emergency welding repairs at night to avoid public panic.

climax.text: Repair crews welded steel plates over every critical joint while workers occupied the building during the day.

punchline.text: A student's homework saved a skyscraper. Nobody knew for 17 years.

quiz.question: How was the Citicorp Tower's flaw discovered?
options: Routine inspection by city building officials
A student's inquiry revealed the structural weakness
Visible cracks appeared after a minor earthquake

details.summary: In 1978, a Princeton student's question revealed that the Citicorp Tower in New York could topple in a quartering wind — a load condition the designer hadn't checked.
details.whyItMatters: The Citicorp Tower story is one of engineering ethics under pressure. LeMessurier chose transparency over cover-up, risking his career to fix a potentially catastrophic flaw — setting a standard for professional responsibility.
takeaways: A student's question revealed the Citicorp Tower's wind vulnerability
The building could have toppled in certain wind conditions
Secret nighttime welding repairs fixed the flaw without public panic

faq.question: What was wrong with the Citicorp Tower?
faq.answer: The tower's unusual stilted base placed columns at the center of each face rather than at corners. When bolted joints replaced original welded connections during construction, the building became vulnerable to quartering winds (45-degree angle) that could cause it to overturn.

faq.question: How was the crisis kept secret?
faq.answer: LeMessurier convinced Citicorp to fund emergency repairs without public disclosure. Welding crews worked nights while office workers occupied the building by day. A news strike helped keep the story quiet. The full account wasn't published until a New Yorker article in 1995.
